title: The Farm-Yard Cock and the Weather-Cock

keywords: the farm-yard cock and the weather-cock
full_text:
The golden weathercock on the church spire looked down at the farmyard cock strutting among the hens: "What a common, noisy bird! He scratches in the dung-heap, whereas I am made of gilded copper and turn only when the great winds blow!"

The farmyard cock flapped his wings and crowed lustily: "Cock-a-doodle-doo! I awaken the farm, I call the sun, and I feed my brood! You sit up in the cold clouds, stiff and hollow, turning whichever way the wind pushes you without a mind of your own!"

A heavy winter gale tore across the steeple, snapping the proud weathercock from his perch and hurling him into the duck pond, while the living rooster gathered his family into the warm coop, safe and purposeful.
moral: Living vitality and purpose surpass high-perched, hollow vanity that turns with every breeze.
